# Exact source charges and separation of earlier originals

22 October 2026. This addresses the REVISE verdict in audit780b9242
of the both-far selected-pair theorem. Its geometric assessment supports
the gain identity, nonstacking, triple-owner correction and automatic
pair-footprint separation. Its proposed charge correction is false
for the supplied original-source constructor. The proof-text objection
about earlier blocks is valid and has been repaired in the E-frontier
note. No independent acceptance is inferred from this response.

## Direct source counts

For R=U(L,10,f) at chart(a-11+r,C+1-c), a and C are odd and all
dimensions even. Its first bar row and leftmost endpoint column are
even. The full two-row bar therefore consists of L/2 physical tiles.
Each leg contributes depth/2 further endpoint tiles, giving

    matching = L+4+f/2,
    endpointTiles = L/2+5+f/2.

The original supports at intrinsic coordinates (0,0) and (0,L+1)
have absolute columns C+1 and C-L. These are respectively in the
next tile to the right and the previous tile to the left of the bar.
Neither far stem nor near stem occupies their tile columns. They are
therefore outside the ENTIRE endpoint tile footprint, not just the bar.
At depth10 the four odd lateral rows3,5,7,9 lie in endpoint tiles;
at depth f the f/2-1 odd lateral rows3,...,f-1 do likewise. Both
axial terminal supports lie in the terminal endpoint tile. Thus

    originalSupportsInside = 4+(f/2-1)+2 = 5+f/2,
    charge(R) = (L+4+f/2)+(5+f/2)-2(L/2+5+f/2) = -1.

For T=U(M,4,g) at chart(a-8+r,s+1-c), the offset is odd/odd.
Its corresponding counts are

    matching = M+1+g/2,
    endpointTiles = M+2+g/2,
    originalSupportsInside = 4+g/2,
    charge(T) = 1-M.

The bar occupies M/2+1 physical tile columns and two physical tile
rows; its leg additions give the displayed endpoint-tile count.
Both original bar-end supports are now inside. The near and far
lateral supports contribute1 and g/2-1, and both axial supports
are inside. Hence the inside count is2+1+(g/2-1)+2=4+g/2.

Both charges are negative. One pair contributes negative mass
1+(M-1)=M and no positive-owner count. The exact selected-pair
Phi identity is unchanged. These counts use immutable original supports,
regardless of which other owners later occupy their locations.

In the audit's concrete triple-owner example, R=U(54,10,26) at
offset(38,2) has matching71, endpointTiles45, insideSupports18:
charge71+18-90=-1. The claimed inside count20 includes the two
outside bar-end supports. T=U(28,4,24) at offset(41,-23) has
matching41, endpointTiles42, insideSupports16 and charge-27.
The pair mass is28, exactly as asserted by the original verifier.
The sharp E witness U(50,10,22) has counts65,41,16 and charge-1.

## Uniform separation from every earlier original

Use the H3 notation and even dimensions of the both-far theorem.
At internal index i, C_i=s_i+w_i+13=s_(i-1)+1 is odd. Partition
the earlier records into the nine base originals B_j, added repair
P_j, west rotor Z_j, south U X_j and the root K.

For every j<i, all B_j endpoints have column at least s_j+2,
including their unbounded long stem. Since offsets decrease, this
is at least s_(i-1)+2=C_i+1. All R endpoints have column at most
C_i. Odd C_i and even C_i+1 lie in different physical tile columns,
so there is no common endpoint tile, mixed full tile or intratile event.
The root has minimum column s_0+w_0+14>=C_i+1 and is separated
by the same argument for arbitrary root breadth.

Earlier P_j,Z_j,X_j may occupy columns at or left of C_i. Their
maximum rows are respectively a_j+2,a_j-1,a_j+2. Since each
anchor gap is at least18, every such endpoint has row at most
a_i-16. R's minimum endpoint row is the even number a_i-11.
Their physical tile rows are therefore strictly smaller than those
of R. This exhausts all earlier originals without any far-leg cutoff.

For R's far strip, the simpler minimum-column bound s_j-4 still
applies. The distinctions above repair the overbroad claim that all
earlier blocks lie to the right. Own-block and first-later-frontier
receipts retain their original proofs and exact sets.

The companion verifier checks the closed-form counts, the exclusion of
both R bar-end supports and inclusion of both T bar-end supports,
and every earlier-owner separation in nonuniform chains. These finite
checks supplement the all-dimension proof. Scoped Lean establishes the
conditional count algebra and the integer physical-row/column bounds;
the source-set counts and chart exhaustion are written arguments.

# Exact old-chain frontier for arbitrary internal E far legs

22 October 2026. Retain every original endpoint, support and matching of
the full H3 chain defined in
[the left-chain exterior theorem](SECONDARY_TEN_LEFT_CHAIN_EXTERIOR.md).
The even dimensions satisfy w_j>=12,z_j>=24, the anchors a_j are odd,
the offsets s_j are even, and

    a_(j+1)=a_j+z_j-6, s_(j+1)=s_j-w_(j+1)-12.

This note removes the E far-leg cutoff for ONE original against H3.
It does not add arbitrary other new owners. The subsequent
[both-far compensation theorem](SECONDARY_TEN_BOTH_FAR_COMPENSATION.md)
uses this frontier and the paired width coupling to prove simultaneous
compensation for arbitrary selected incident-ten pairs.

## Statement

Fix an internal index i>=1 and a full original

    R=U(L,10,f), chart(r,c)=(a_i-11+r,C_i+1-c),
    C_i=s_i+w_i+13, L>=w_i+20, f>=4, L,f even.

The width condition is necessary whenever R is an actual E owner with
incident ten: the actual-owner coupling gives L>=w_i+M+14 with M>=6.
For the present theorem, completeness is unnecessary; R need only be
endpoint-disjoint from H3. Its even far column and terminal row are

    F=C_i+1-L<=s_i-6, b=a_i-11+f.

Let k>i be the first index with F>=s_k-4, if it exists. The following
table is exact. The deduction d is defined only on the legal rows.

| Far column | Endpoint-disjoint iff | Deduction d |
|---|---|---|
| No k | Every even f>=4 | 0 |
| F=s_k-4 | b<=a_k-3 | 0 |
| F=s_k-2 | b<=a_k-3 | 1 if b=a_k-3, otherwise 0 |
| F=s_k | b<=a_k-5 | 2 if b is a_k-7 or a_k-5, otherwise 0 |
| s_k+2<=F<=s_(k-1)-6 | b<=a_k-9 | 1 if b=a_k-9, otherwise 0 |

For every legal R,

    Phi(H3 union {R})-Phi(H3)=1-d>=-1.                 (1)

The minimum -1 occurs exactly in the third finite-contact row with
b in {a_k-7,a_k-5}. It is attained by endpoint-disjoint originals.
These witnesses need not admit a complete extension. A negative R
marginal neither refutes a joint-pair compensation rule nor the global
target inequality.

## First-contact proof

Every old block, including its P,Z,X originals, has minimum endpoint
column s_j-4. The far strip of R uses the physical tile column {F,F+1}.
For j<=i, F<=s_i-6 puts that tile strictly to the left of every old
endpoint. If k exists, minimality and even parity give

    s_k-4<=F<=s_(k-1)-6.

Every block before k is separated from the far strip by the same
tile-column argument. Separation of the fixed bar and near leg needs
a different argument. Write B_j for the nine base originals, P_j for
the added U repair, Z_j for the west rotor and X_j for the south U.
For j<i, every B_j endpoint has column at least s_j+2, hence at least
s_(i-1)+2=C_i+1. The root original has minimum column s_0+w_0+14,
also at least C_i+1. R has maximum column C_i; since C_i is odd, these
sets lie across a physical tile-column boundary. Earlier P_j,Z_j,X_j
need not lie to the right: instead their maximum endpoint rows are at
most a_j+2<=a_i-16. R starts at the even row a_i-11, so their physical
tile rows are strictly above every R endpoint. This proves separation
from ALL earlier originals, including unbounded earlier base stems.

The R bar is above its own P bar and every later block. Its fixed
near leg has the same four-full-tile/eight-event receipt as in the
short-pair theorem; the own-block calculation is unchanged by f.
Extending its far leg therefore changes only the strip at {F,F+1}.

Substitution in the full original charts of block k gives the first
same-column endpoint and the relevant partner-column profile:

| F | First old endpoint in column F | Relevant endpoints at F+1 |
|---|---|---|
| s_k-4 | X_k at row a_k-2 | None before the legal terminal tile |
| s_k-2 | Z_k at row a_k-2 | Z_k starts at row a_k-4 |
| s_k | Z_k at row a_k-3 | P_k far stem at rows a_k-8,...,a_k-4 |
| F>=s_k+2 | P_k bar at row a_k-8 | None above that bar |

R occupies every far-column row from a_i-11 through b. Its start is
above each displayed first endpoint. Avoiding that endpoint, with b
even, gives exactly the legal bounds in the statement. In particular
the last case is blocked by the P BAR, even when another old stem
continues farther down. Treating that stem as the first obstacle would
give an incorrect legal depth.

These bounds are sufficient as well. R's bar and near leg have already
been separated; earlier blocks cannot meet the far tile column. All
legal terminals satisfy b<=a_k-3. Every block after k starts at row at
least a_(k+1)-8>=a_k+10, below this terminal and its physical tile.
There is no later block when k is last. If k does not exist, column
separation excludes every old endpoint and intratile receipt for any f.
This proves the exact collision table without a depth or chain cutoff.

## Exact physical receipts

All coordinates below are absolute. A physical tile is specified by
its even top-left coordinate; rows increase downward. Old supports stay
excluded from directed events even if another owner consumes them.

The near receipt has four new mixed full tiles and eight new directed
events, hence signed value zero. R has charge -1 and adds negative
mass one. For clarity, the direct original-source counts are

    matching(R)=L+4+f/2,
    endpointTiles(R)=L/2+5+f/2,
    originalSupportsInside(R)=5+f/2.

Both supports at the ends of the aligned bar, chart(0,0) and
chart(0,L+1), lie OUTSIDE its endpoint tile footprint. The two leg
axial supports lie inside; the lateral supports inside number
10/2-1 and f/2-1. Thus the inside count is 2+4+(f/2-1)=5+f/2,
not 7+f/2, and the charge is exactly -1. The far receipt is disjoint
from these near tiles.

At F=s_k-4, even the last legal terminal b=a_k-3 creates no event:
R's downward target is its original axial support, and X_k's upward
target is X_k's original axial support. There is no mixed full tile.

At F=s_k-2, only b=a_k-3 activates a receipt. The tile with top-left
(a_k-3,F) has R at its upper-left cell and Z_k at the other three.
The two horizontal directions at row b and the upward Z_k direction
from (b+1,F) survive. R's downward direction is excluded by its axial
support. Thus there is one new mixed full tile and three new events,
with signed value -1. Earlier even terminals create no receipt.

At F=s_k, activation occurs at b=a_k-7 or a_k-5. Write

    b=a_k-7+2h, h in {0,1}.

The new mixed full tiles have top-left (a_k-7,F) when h=1 and none
when h=0. For each t=0,...,h the events are exactly

    R:(a_k-7+2t,F) -> P_k:(a_k-7+2t,F+1),
    P_k:(a_k-7+2t,F+1) -> R:(a_k-7+2t,F).

At odd rows the horizontal directions target original supports of the
respective originals. The entry tile, where P_k first occupies its
lower-right cell, has no event or full tile. The terminal tile has the
two displayed events and lacks R's lower-left cell. Therefore the far
receipt has h new mixed full tiles and 2h+2 events, signed value -2.
All earlier terminals have zero far receipt. Z_k in the same column
prevents any continuation to X_k or another later profile.

In the remaining column range only b=a_k-9 activates a receipt. There
is a single upward event P_k:(b+1,F)->R:(b,F); R's reverse direction
targets its original axial support. The partner cells are absent, so
there is no new full tile. The signed value is -1.

These profiles exhaust the legal far strip. Adding its signed value
to the near value zero and mass one proves (1). Every mixed full tile
and owner-labelled event is counted as a physical set element once.
No old-prefix reserve or other new owner's negative mass is used.

## A sharp local witness and the remaining simultaneous problem

Take a_0=31,s_0=0, three blocks with all w_j=12,z_j=24 and root
breadth six. At i=1, a_i=49,s_i=-24,C_i=1. Let

    R=U(50,10,22), chart(r,c)=(38+r,2-c).

Then F=-48=s_2 and b=60=a_2-7. R is endpoint-disjoint from H3 and
has exact increment -1. Its actual forced t partner, if it exists,
has left incident four and width at most 24 by the coupling inequality.
The witness alone is not a complete configuration or a counterexample
to simultaneous pair gain >=4m.

The frontier theorem proves that a long R can lose at most two units
to the OLD chain. A discovery run checked 18,111 marginals against
H3 plus selected new T owners with minimum -1; this finite observation
is not a proof of joint compensation. The subsequent both-far theorem
proves the necessary nonstacking using the coupled frontiers and gives
an aligned-bar argument separating entire pairs. Its general proof and
separate validation, rather than this discovery run, establish that
selected-union strengthening.

The companion verifier checks exact collision decisions and complete
mixed-full-tile and owner-labelled-event SETS at every frontier phase,
translated and nonuniform chains, and large far depths. The standalone
Lean module checks the frontier parity arithmetic, conditional receipt
identity and sharp lower bound. Full original geometric exhaustion is
the written proof above; it is not claimed to be fully formalized.

Validation passed 19,712 collision decisions and 10,482 exact full/event
set comparisons, with all four frontier phases and far depths up to 2000.
Local standalone Lean passed 18 declarations, including 17 theorems;
individual axiom reports contain only ordinary axioms, with no warnings,
sorry or native axioms. No independent review of this new frontier theorem
has been submitted or accepted as a standalone question. This frontier IS
included as a necessary dependency in the separate both-far audit780b9242.
The earlier arbitrary-t-far audit ended in infrastructure failure with no
mathematical verdict and did not include this frontier.
See the [validation record](../output/secondary-ten-e-far-frontier-validation.json).

The global 5/6 improvement, full-family allocation and rectangular-grid
triple equality remain open. The submitted 11 October manuscript stays
unchanged.

def independent_source(parameters, symmetry, offset):
    width, left, right = parameters
    matching = [((0, column), (0, column+1)) for column in range(1, width, 2)]
    matching += [((1, column), (1, column+1)) for column in range(2, width-1, 2)]
    matching += [((row, column), (row+1, column))
                 for column, height in ((1, left), (width, right)) for row in range(1, height, 2)]
    support = {(0, 0), (0, width+1), (left+1, 1), (right+1, width)}
    support |= {(row, 0 if row % 2 == 0 else 2) for row in range(2, left+1)}
    support |= {(row, width+1 if row % 2 == 0 else width-1) for row in range(2, right+1)}
    move = lambda point: affine(point, symmetry, offset)
    return ({move(point) for edge in matching for point in edge},
            {move(point) for point in support},
            {tuple(sorted((move(first), move(second)))) for first, second in matching})

"""Direct original-support charge counts and complete earlier-owner separation."""

import itertools
import json

from check_demand_hull_reserve_obstruction import independent_source
from check_incident_eight_north_transfer import charge
from check_secondary_ten_arbitrary_t_consumers import old_chain


if not __debug__:
    raise RuntimeError('Run without -O: verification uses assertions.')


def counts(record):
    tiles = {(row//2, column//2) for row, column in record[0]}
    inside = {point for point in record[1] if (point[0]//2, point[1]//2) in tiles}
    return len(record[2]), len(tiles), len(inside)


def main():
    receiver_controls = consumer_controls = separated = 0
    for breadth, far, anchor, column in itertools.product(
            (6, 28, 54, 200), (4, 22, 26, 2000), (-33, 31, 49), (-101, 1, 201)):
        receiver = independent_source((breadth, 10, far), (False, False, True),
                                      (anchor-11, column+1))
        assert counts(receiver) == (breadth+4+far//2,
                                   breadth//2+5+far//2, 5+far//2)
        tiles = {(row//2, value//2) for row, value in receiver[0]}
        assert all((point[0]//2, point[1]//2) not in tiles
                   for point in ((anchor-11, column+1), (anchor-11, column-breadth)))
        assert charge(receiver) == -1
        receiver_controls += 1
        consumer = independent_source((breadth, 4, far), (False, False, True),
                                      (anchor-8, column))
        assert counts(consumer) == (breadth+1+far//2,
                                   breadth+2+far//2, 4+far//2)
        tiles = {(row//2, value//2) for row, value in consumer[0]}
        assert all((point[0]//2, point[1]//2) in tiles
                   for point in ((anchor-8, column), (anchor-8, column-breadth-1)))
        assert charge(consumer) == 1-breadth
        consumer_controls += 1
    for anchor, offset, root in itertools.product((-33, 31), (-100, 0, 200), (6, 200)):
        widths = [12, 14, 20, 18, 30, 12, 50]
        depths = [24, 26, 40, 2000, 80, 24, 28]
        records, bases, unused, sites = old_chain(anchor, offset, widths, depths, root)
        size = len(sites)
        for index in range(1, size):
            origin, unused, lateral = sites[index]
            near_column = lateral+widths[index]+13
            assert near_column == sites[index-1][2]+1
            for earlier in range(index):
                for record in bases[earlier]:
                    assert min(column for row, column in record[0]) >= near_column+1
                    separated += 1
                for position in (9*size+1+earlier, 10*size+1+earlier, 11*size+1+earlier):
                    assert max(row for row, column in records[position][0]) <= origin-16
                    assert max(row//2 for row, column in records[position][0]) < (origin-11)//2
                    separated += 1
            assert min(column for row, column in records[9*size][0]) >= near_column+1
            separated += 1
    print(json.dumps(dict(status='PASS', receiver_charge_controls=receiver_controls,
        consumer_charge_controls=consumer_controls, earlier_original_controls=separated,
        scope='Exact immutable-support counts refute the proposed R positive-charge '
              'correction. General count and earlier-owner separation proofs are written; '
              'finite controls do not prove catalogue exhaustion or global allocation.'), indent=2))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()


The affine map applies sign flips before transposition: transpose,flip_row,flip_column=symmetry; row,column=point; row=-row if flip_row else row; column=-column if flip_column else column; if transpose: row,column=column,row; return row+offset[0],column+offset[1]. north_U(origin,offset,breadth,depth,far,left) calls independent_source((breadth,depth,far),(False,False,left),(origin-4-depth,offset+1 if left else offset-1)). charge is len(matching)+len({support in originalSupport with supportTile in endpointTiles})-2*len(endpointTiles). Standalone local tests:144Rcounts,144Tcounts,3096earlierOriginalSeparations PASS; nine scoped Lean theorems individually ordinary-axiom audited, no warnings/sorry/native.
